players.product: Apple Silicon (A19 / A19 Pro, M5) — leading-edge logic on TSMC N2/N3

quarterly_data.signal: June-quarter (Q3 FY2026) results by category, per CEO Cook and CFO Parekh: products revenue $78.7 billion, up 18% year over year, 'driven by double-digit growth on iPhone and Mac'; iPhone $54.3 billion, up 22% ('driven by the iPhone 17 family'; June-quarter records in every geographic segment and a June-quarter record for upgraders); services $30.7 billion, up 12% (a June-quarter record 'despite significant sequential foreign exchange headwinds'); iPad $6.2 billion, down 6% ('driven by the continued difficult compare against the launch of the A16-powered iPad in the prior year'); wearables, home and accessories $7.9 billion, up 6%. Net income $29.8 billion; diluted EPS 'included $0.11 of favorable impact from tariff refunds'; operating cash flow $34.4 billion. CFO: net income, EPS and operating cash flow 'set June quarter records, even when excluding the tariff refund benefit.' Installed base of 'over two and a half billion active devices'; services have 'surpassed one and a half billion in paid subscriptions'.
quarterly_data.figure: iPhone $54.3 billion (+22%); Services $30.7 billion (+12%); Products $78.7 billion (+18%); iPad $6.2 billion (-6%); net income $29.8 billion; tariff refunds $0.11 of EPS

quarterly_data.signal: September-quarter (Q4 FY2026) outlook items beyond the headline guide, CFO Parekh: services year-over-year reported growth 'to be largely similar to what we reported in the June quarter after removing the negative sequential impact of about two and a half percentage points from foreign exchange'; for services, foreign exchange is expected to drive 'about a 5 percentage point headwind to the year-over-year growth rate from the March to September quarter' ('this is a theme that's impacting the services business more so than the total company'); OI&E around $350 million, excluding any potential impact from the mark to market of minority investments. The outlook 'assumes that global tariff rates, policies, and their application remain in effect as of this call, and the global macroeconomic outlook does not worsen from today.' Beyond September: 'we're not providing any kind of color or guidance beyond the September quarter.'
quarterly_data.figure: services growth largely similar to June after about two and a half points of FX; services FX headwind about 5 percentage points (March to September quarter); OI&E around $350 million

quarterly_data.signal: Services drivers, CFO Parekh: from 16% services growth in the March quarter to 12% in the June quarter, 'foreign exchange was the main driver for the change in the year-over-year growth rate sequentially'; the year-ago June and September quarters carried the favorable impact of the F1 theatrical release, with no theatrical release this year; the App Store 'did see some headwinds in mobile gaming', Apple 'made some changes to the App Store business model in certain countries', and in the U.S. 'we do continue to operate under a court ruling impacting the link-out transactions. We're pleased the Supreme Court will hear our appeal.' The App Store still set a June-quarter revenue record; cloud services, video, payment services and advertising grew strong double digits, every services category set a revenue record, with all-time records in cloud services and payment services (Apple Pay at a record level of users). Versus Apple's own June-quarter expectations: 'we roughly met our expectations, but we did see a bit more softness on mobile gaming in the App Store.'
quarterly_data.figure: services +12% in the June quarter vs 16% in the March quarter; App Store June-quarter record despite mobile gaming headwinds

quarterly_data.signal: Demand and pricing views, CEO Cook: asked whether demand was pulled forward, he said iPhone has been 'running at this 22% growth rate for the last while... It's not obvious in the data that what you're asking is true.' On how Apple sets prices: 'we look at units, revenue, and margin, then come to a business judgment as to how to handle that. It's not a mathematical formula... We look at all three dimensions and think about it over the long term, instead of a 90-day clock.' CFO Parekh for the September quarter: 'On iPhone, we expect to continue to see high levels of demand.'
quarterly_data.figure: iPhone up 22% year to date; pull-forward not evident in the data (CEO)

quarterly_data.signal: Siri AI economics, CEO Cook: on compute cost, 'it's obviously early going for us. I don't want to say that we have a complete plan for that.' 'We do believe there will be people that want to use it a lot. We will have some kind of upgrade possibilities on iCloud+ where people can buy up the stack on iCloud+. We'll see how the pickup for that is.' Later: 'There's also the ability when people use it a lot for them to move up on an iCloud Plan as well. What the balance of that is a bit uncertain at the moment.' On AI opportunities: 'the ability to run some percentage of request on device is also very strategic and sort of a competitive weapon, if you will.'

MacBook Neo and enterprise / education demand: CEO Cook - MacBook Neo 'has been especially popular... we're continuing to work hard to meet demand'; Mac set an all-time revenue record in emerging markets and in Greater China, and all-time records for upgraders and customers new to Mac. CFO Parekh: in the last quarter 'about half of the MacBook Neo large purchases by U.S. education institutions displaced Windows and Chromebook devices' - Pinellas County Schools (Florida) is transitioning 25,000 students from Windows devices to MacBook Neo, Peninsula School District 401 (Washington) moved over 8,000 students from Chromebooks to MacBook Neo, and Midwest City-Del City School District (Oklahoma) purchased over 6,000 MacBook Neos; in enterprise, Morgan Stanley has deployed over 20,000 iPhone 17 devices, and Credit Agricole uses on-device AI on MacBook Pro for regulatory workflows, 'reducing manual processing time by over 80%'.
quarterly_data.figure: about half of U.S. education MacBook Neo large purchases displaced Windows / Chromebook devices; 25,000 students (Pinellas County); over 20,000 iPhone 17 devices (Morgan Stanley)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Cook: Apple announced 'Apple Upgrade' in the week of the call for customers in the U.S. - 'a new hardware leasing program launched in partnership with Klarna' to make it easier for customers to get Apple's latest products; it is offered in Apple's retail stores and 'not widely offered in all channels', and CFO Parekh added it is 'only available in the U.S. right now'. Cook: residual values on Apple products 'are generally much higher than the residual value on several of our competition', and 'the early feedback on it is quite positive.'
